yields_resource: A route back to town from deep in the dungeon, with access to trade and recovery.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: On the ninth level, the stairs to town lead to a cave near where Wirt stands. It is the deep delver's way home, and it opens right beside a figure who profits from the desperate.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it as the mid-to-late dungeon exit. It consumes the party's depleted resources and feeds Wirt-style trade scenes and tension about what the deep sends after them. An arrival goes well when the party emerges unpursued and bargains wisely. It goes badly when they are chased, drained of supplies, or pressed into a poor deal.

title: Cavern Levels
summary: The cave-like middle depths of the dungeon. Lava lakes squeeze the footing into narrow paths, Poison Spitters hold the open ground, and big hordes have room to run. Ranged attackers can also keep their distance here, so the usual doorway trick fails.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a one-shot fighting retreat across a lava-lit cave. The party must thin or evade a huge horde while Poison Spitters pepper them from range, and the only safe footing is a few narrow paths between lava lakes. Success means reaching the far side of the cave. Staying put means being overrun.
premise: A hero who relies on thinning hordes from a safe position + a cavern with no doorways to hide behind and enemies who keep their distance = a fight that is won by movement and nerve, not by attrition.

sensory.physical_environment: Cave-like middle levels where lava lakes become common and leave only narrow paths between them.
sensory.behaviors: Poison Spitters are common. Monsters arrive in large hordes, often with generally slower monsters in tow, and ranged enemies have room to run and keep their distance.
sensory.relationships: Spitters and their slower companions move together, and the horde works as one pressure. The Rogue fights here but is badly matched to its scale.
sensory.attitudes: The cave offers no mercy and no chokepoint. Everything is in the open and pressing in.
sensory.values: Space, range and mobility matter more than patience. Thinning the horde takes accuracy the hero may not have.

establishment.name: The monster hordes of the Cavern
establishment.worldview: The open cave belongs to numbers. Overwhelm whatever walks in.
establishment.leverage: Sheer mass, room to run, and ranged Spitters that need no doorway.
establishment.flaw: The slower monsters trail behind the fast ones, so the horde arrives in uneven waves.

main_opponent.name: The Rogue
main_opponent.worldview: Distance and precision decide a fight.
main_opponent.leverage: Ranged skill, and the chance to draw foes through chokepoints elsewhere in the dungeon.
main_opponent.flaw: Here the doorway trick fails, and thinning a horde takes very reliable accuracy.

thematic_shadow.name: Poison Spitters
thematic_shadow.worldview: The best fight is the one where you are never touched.
thematic_shadow.leverage: They hold range in open cave and can pick off anyone caught on a narrow path.
thematic_shadow.flaw: They rely on the slower brutes to screen them, and they are fragile if reached.

tertiary_outcast.name: A lone survivor stranded on a lava-locked ledge
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Nobody crosses the Cavern twice without a reason.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Knows which narrow paths still hold.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Cut off, short of supplies, and watched by every Spitter in range.

output_dial.level_1: A cautious crossing of the lava paths, with a few Spitters and slow-moving monsters that can be handled one at a time.
output_dial.level_2: A real horde gathers, Spitters keep their range, and the party has to fight while moving along narrow paths.
output_dial.level_3: Hordes flood the open ground, ranged fire pins the party on the lava paths, and retreat is cut off.
output_dial.level_4: The party is surrounded on a shrinking path, poison and lava close in together, and only a sacrifice or a desperate breakout survives.

threat_clocks.name: The horde closes
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party stands and trades fire in the open instead of moving or finding a defensible path.

threat_clocks.name: Poison saturation
threat_clocks.advances_when: Spitters get uncontested ranged volleys onto the party's position.

yields_resource: Safe passage to the deeper dungeon, plus knowledge of which narrow lava paths hold, which can be reused as a defensible route.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The Cavern levels are the point where the dungeon stops funneling the party into corridors. Lava lakes carve narrow paths, hordes run freely and Poison Spitters keep range. The hero who relied on doorways and patience now faces an open fight that demands accuracy, mobility and nerve.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it in the middle of a descent, after tight-corridor levels have taught the party to rely on chokepoints. It consumes the party's assumption that distance attackers can be pulled through a doorway, and it feeds deeper levels with a worn-down, wary party. Use the lava paths as the main tactical feature. An arrival goes well when the party plans a route, uses the paths as their own chokepoints and picks off Spitters. It goes badly when they linger in the open or expect a doorway to save them.

title: Caves
summary: An area reached by descending the dungeon. Arriving here opens another entrance to the surface, giving the party a new way out and back.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a cavern region that the party has pushed deep enough to reach, where discovering a second route to the surface changes how they resupply, retreat and plan.
premise: A delver committed to going deeper + a new exit opening at the caves = a choice between retreating to safety and descending further.

sensory.physical_environment: A cavernous area deep in the dungeon, with another entrance leading up to the surface.
sensory.behaviors: Delvers weigh whether to return to the surface or continue onward.
sensory.relationships: The caves connect the dungeon to the surface world above.
sensory.attitudes: Relief at a second way out, tempered by what lies deeper.
sensory.values: Access, retreat and the freedom to choose when to go on.

establishment.name: Those who hold the surface
establishment.worldview: The way back must stay open and orderly.
establishment.leverage: Supplies and refuge at the surface end of the route.
establishment.flaw: They are distant from the danger below.

main_opponent.name: Whatever dwells in the caves
main_opponent.worldview: The caves are its territory, and a new entrance changes nothing for it.
main_opponent.leverage: Knows the terrain and can threaten the route.
main_opponent.flaw: Bound to the place.

thematic_shadow.name: A delver who never goes back up
thematic_shadow.worldview: The surface is behind them and only descent matters.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Shows the cost of ignoring the exit.
thematic_shadow.flaw: Exhaustion and isolation.

tertiary_outcast.name: A scavenger using the new entrance
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Every opening is an opportunity.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Knows who comes and goes.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Unreliable and exposed.

output_dial.level_1: The party reaches the caves and finds the new exit, an easy chance to resupply and return.
output_dial.level_2: The new route helps, but the party must decide whether to use it or keep descending.
output_dial.level_3: The new entrance exposes the route to threats, so going up or down both carry risk.
output_dial.level_4: The second entrance proves a trap or a conduit, and the route to safety is cut off just when the party needs it most.

threat_clocks.name: Route Compromised
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party leaves the new entrance unattended or draws pursuers toward it.

yields_resource: A second entrance to the surface, shortening retreat and resupply.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: Reaching the caves opens another entrance to the surface. The place is a waypoint and a decision, a moment when the party can step back toward the world above or press deeper.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it as a midpoint of a descent, where the party has earned a breather. It consumes the party's progress and feeds their options for retreat, resupply and pacing. It connects directly to the surface. It pairs well with hazards found within cave-like levels. An arrival goes well when the party uses the exit wisely to recover and return stronger. It goes badly when the party assumes the route is safe, or when the new entrance lets danger travel the other way. The card says nothing about what lies inside the caves, so inhabitants and hazards are the GM's addition.

title: Chamber of Bone
summary: A dungeon area built around a main room. The source only hints that its surroundings behave differently under infravision, so the rest is left for the table to fill in.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a one-room crawl. The party reaches a bone-strewn main chamber and finds that heat-sight or similar darkvision reveals something different outside the room than inside it. They decide whether to investigate the difference or leave.
premise: Curious explorers who trust their special senses + a chamber that looks different once they step outside its main room = a discovery they cannot unsee, or a trap they walked into.

sensory.physical_environment: A main room of piled bone, with the passages beyond it dark and strange to sight.
sensory.behaviors: Explorers test their darkvision at the edge of the main room and compare what they see inside and outside.
sensory.relationships: The chamber stands apart from the rest of the dungeon. Its main room is the anchor, and the outer area is the part to be probed.
sensory.attitudes: Playful curiosity, as the source's "for grins" suggests, shading into unease.
sensory.values: Experimentation, observation, and the nerve to look at what others avoid.

establishment.name: The delvers' conventional wisdom
establishment.worldview: The main room is the place that matters, so clear it and move on.
establishment.leverage: It offers a simple, proven route through the chamber.
establishment.flaw: It never looks at the periphery, where the difference is.

main_opponent.name: Whatever lurks beyond the main room
main_opponent.worldview: The chamber's secrets are meant to be found only by those who look the wrong way.
main_opponent.leverage: Darkness, the unexpected, and the main room's distraction.
main_opponent.flaw: It is revealed by the same senses it exploits.

thematic_shadow.name: The over-curious scout
thematic_shadow.worldview: Every sense must be tested and every oddity poked.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Willingness to try what others will not.
thematic_shadow.flaw: Recklessness, because the reward is unknown.

tertiary_outcast.name: The skittish survivor
tertiary_outcast.worldview: The chamber should be left alone.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Memory of what went wrong for earlier visitors.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Fear keeps the warnings vague, so nobody can act on them.

output_dial.level_1: The chamber is an eerie bone-filled room, and the infravision trick is only a curious quirk.
output_dial.level_2: The oddity outside the main room points to a real hidden feature that the party must work around.
output_dial.level_3: The hidden feature turns hostile and the party is caught between the room and the dark beyond.
output_dial.level_4: What the chamber concealed breaks loose and the party must flee or be buried among the bones.

threat_clocks.name: The Chamber Notices
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party lingers, probes the periphery, or makes noise in or around the main room.

yields_resource: A revealed secret about the chamber's layout or hidden contents, plus safe knowledge of how to see what others miss.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The canon gives only a hint: the main room is notable, and infravision used outside it is worth trying. Treat the room as a bone-heavy anchor, and let the strangeness live in the surrounding space, where sight does not behave as the party expects. Everything beyond that hint is a GM judgement.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it as a short side detour deep in a dungeon, after the party has settled into relying on their senses. It consumes a Dark-Sight-Method and feeds Lore or a hazard that the next scene can use. It goes well when the party experiments and learns something. It goes badly when they treat the main room as the whole chamber and walk into what the periphery was hiding.

title: Character Class Philosophy
summary: The guide's view that the three hero classes are archetypes, that the Sorcerer is the pivot point of character abilities, and that players should build a primary and a secondary configuration instead of specializing narrowly.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a short mentor scene where a veteran advises the party to prepare a second approach for foes their usual method cannot handle. The scene ends with each hero naming a backup method they will cultivate.
premise: Heroes who lean on a single proven style + foes that shrug it off = a lesson in cultivating a second approach.

sensory.physical_environment: A hero's gear, skills and spells laid out side by side, reflecting a primary and a secondary configuration.
sensory.behaviors: Players experiment outside their comfort class and plan a fallback.
sensory.relationships: Three archetypes, Warrior, Rogue and Sorcerer, relate as distinct talents that can each borrow from the others.
sensory.attitudes: Treat the character as having a split personality, and refuse to be a one-trick pony.
sensory.values: Versatility, replayability, and the fun found by experimenting beyond one class.

establishment.name: The three archetypes
establishment.worldview: Warrior, Rogue and Sorcerer are uniquely talented heroes with an inherent ability that dictates the best fighting style.
establishment.leverage: Each has a clear strength that makes play legible and effective.
establishment.flaw: Leaning only on that inherent strength leaves the hero exposed.

main_opponent.name: Foes immune to a hero's usual attack
main_opponent.worldview: Some enemies cannot be handled by non-magical combat alone.
main_opponent.leverage: They punish a character built too narrowly.
main_opponent.flaw: They fall to a hero who has prepared a second, magical option.

thematic_shadow.name: The one-trick pony
thematic_shadow.worldview: Pour everything into a couple of traits and be superb at one thing.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Great strength in a single narrow area.
thematic_shadow.flaw: Total failure when that area does not apply.

tertiary_outcast.name: The player who never leaves the Warrior class
tertiary_outcast.worldview: The familiar path is enough.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Reliable mastery of a single style.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Misses two-thirds of the fun.

output_dial.level_1: A hero is comfortable in their main style and a second option is a pleasant extra.
output_dial.level_2: The party meets a foe that resists their main approach and must lean on a secondary option.
output_dial.level_3: A narrowly built hero is stranded against enemies they cannot hurt, and the party scrambles to compensate.
output_dial.level_4: An over-specialized party meets an enemy their only methods cannot touch, forcing retreat or ruin.

threat_clocks.name: Over-Specialization Exposed
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party meets foes their primary method cannot handle and has no fallback ready.

yields_resource: A shared understanding of how to build a flexible hero, giving the party a secondary approach before it is needed.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The guide treats the three classes as archetypes, with Sorcery as the pivot point of character abilities. Any class can develop the strengths of the others to a lesser extent. Heroes should keep a primary and a secondary configuration and avoid pouring everything into a couple of traits. Warrior and Rogue are alike in purely non-magical combat, so both should cultivate a magical attack.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place early in a campaign as a mentor scene or between delves, then reinforce it with an encounter that punishes narrow builds. It consumes a quiet moment and feeds the Magical Resistance situation, since resistant foes are exactly where a secondary configuration matters. Arrival goes well if heroes diversify and test a backup. It goes badly if they cling to one method and meet an enemy that renders it useless.

title: Crypt in the Graveyard
summary: A crypt in Tristram's graveyard where the stairway from the fifth dungeon level emerges, giving delvers a way back to town.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a one-shot: the party climbs out of a lower dungeon through a crypt into a quiet graveyard above a frightened village, and must decide whether to rest, resupply and return below or seal the way behind them.
premise: Delvers who need to recover + a way home that opens onto the dead = relief shadowed by the thing they left below.

sensory.physical_environment: A crypt in Tristram's graveyard; stairways rise out of it from the dungeon below.
sensory.behaviors: Weary adventurers climb out toward the town; villagers avoid the graveyard.
sensory.relationships: The crypt ties the dungeon's fifth level to Tristram, linking the buried horror to the people above.
sensory.attitudes: Relief at reaching the surface mixed with unease at what the crypt lets out or lets in.
sensory.values: Return, recovery and the thin line between the living town and what lies beneath it.

establishment.name: Tristram
establishment.worldview: The town wants the graveyard quiet and its heroes returning alive.
establishment.leverage: Shelter, trade and healing waiting at the top of the stairs.
establishment.flaw: It cannot defend the crypt itself and depends on outsiders.

main_opponent.name: The dungeon's denizens
main_opponent.worldview: The passage runs both ways and the dead have a claim on the surface.
main_opponent.leverage: The stairway offers them a path to the town.
main_opponent.flaw: They are drawn to the route and can be ambushed or sealed off at it.

thematic_shadow.name: A returning delver
thematic_shadow.worldview: Retreat is wisdom, not cowardice.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Knows exactly what waits below the crypt.
thematic_shadow.flaw: Brings the dungeon's taint back up with them.

tertiary_outcast.name: A graveyard watcher
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Someone must keep vigil over the crypt, whatever the town prefers.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Sees who and what climbs out, and when.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Isolated, doubted and easily silenced.

output_dial.level_1: The crypt is a quiet, reliable exit and the party passes through to town unmolested.
output_dial.level_2: The stairway is usable, but the graveyard stirs uneasily and the party must move carefully.
output_dial.level_3: Something follows the party up the stairs and the crypt becomes a fight to protect the town.
output_dial.level_4: The crypt becomes a breach and the dungeon's horrors pour into Tristram's graveyard and the town beyond.

threat_clocks.name: Breach at the Crypt
threat_clocks.advances_when: Delvers flee upward with pursuers, the crypt goes unguarded, or the dead are disturbed.

yields_resource: A safe way back to town to heal, resupply and regroup, plus knowledge of what is stirring below.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The fifth level of the dungeon has stairways rising into the crypt in Tristram's graveyard, opening a route to the town. It is both lifeline and weak point: a way home for the party and a door for whatever follows.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it as the first reliable exit after the early dungeon descent. It consumes the party's need for rest and supplies, and feeds Tristram's scenes of recovery, trade and rumor. An arrival goes well when the party reaches the crypt unpursued and uses the town to prepare. It goes badly when pursuers follow them up, or when retreat becomes habit and the town starts to bear the cost.

title: The Tavern Keeper's Plea: The Curse of King Leoric
summary: In the Tristram tavern, Ogden recounts the tragic tale of King Leoric and begs the hero to destroy the king's cursed form and free his soul.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a single tavern scene. A frightened innkeeper tells of a king who rose from the grave in a cursed body and pleads with the party to end his torment. The scene closes when the party accepts or refuses, and the innkeeper points them toward the king's resting place.
premise: A decent man who cannot fight + a beloved dead king walking cursed = he must beg a stranger to give the king peace.

sensory.physical_environment: The tavern in Tristram, a small and shaken town. Lamplight, low voices, and a keeper who lowers his voice to tell the old tale.
sensory.behaviors: Ogden implores the hero, speaking with reverence and grief about a king he cannot help himself.
sensory.relationships: A townsman asks a stranger to settle a matter of loyalty to a former ruler. The king is both a lost sovereign and a danger.
sensory.attitudes: Pity for the king and fear of what he has become, joined by a sense that the dead should be at peace.
sensory.values: Mercy toward the dead, duty to a fallen lord, and the hope that destruction can be a kindness.

establishment.name: Ogden the Tavern Owner
establishment.worldview: A decent townsman who believes the king's soul deserves rest and that someone brave must give it.
establishment.leverage: Local trust, the knowledge of the king's story, and the standing to direct the hero.
establishment.flaw: He is no fighter. He can only plead and hope the stranger will act.

main_opponent.name: King Leoric (cursed)
main_opponent.worldview: A once-noble ruler now bound in a cursed form, with no peace to be had.
main_opponent.leverage: His undead power, and his ability to raise an army of bones.
main_opponent.flaw: He is trapped by the curse and cannot choose to stop.

thematic_shadow.name: The unquiet dead of Tristram
thematic_shadow.worldview: Those who cannot rest are a symptom of the corruption beneath the town.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Fear, which spreads through the town as rumor.
thematic_shadow.flaw: They are echoes without will and cannot bargain.

tertiary_outcast.name: A townsperson who would rather leave the king undisturbed
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Some things are better left buried, and a hero may only make them worse.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Gossip and discouragement that sow doubt about the quest.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Their caution offers no answer to the threat.

output_dial.level_1: The tale is told over a quiet drink and the party takes it as an interesting piece of local history.
output_dial.level_2: Ogden makes a heartfelt appeal, and the party takes on the task of laying the king to rest.
output_dial.level_3: The plea is desperate, the townsfolk are afraid, and refusing the task means the curse spreads unchecked.
output_dial.level_4: The cursed king's horde reaches the town itself, and the tale becomes a warning of what the party failed to prevent.

threat_clocks.name: The Unquiet King
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party delays or refuses, and rumors of the cursed king's movements grow.

yields_resource: A clear mandate from the townsfolk, the story of the king's fall, and the direction to his tomb.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: Ogden the Tavern Owner tells the tragic story of King Leoric and implores the hero to destroy his cursed form so that his soul may be at ease. It is a quest hook driven by pity as much as fear.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it in a tavern or common room early in a campaign, once the party has reached the town. It consumes the party's willingness to help and feeds directly into the tomb encounter, where the king can actually be destroyed. It goes well when the grief in the telling gives the fight a moral weight. It goes badly if it is delivered as a plain job offer, or if the party ignores the plea and the king's threat grows unopposed.

title: The Cursed Cathedral
summary: The church in Tristram. Its front door is the main entrance to the dungeon and leads down to the first level of the labyrinth.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a one-shot threshold scene. The party stands at the front door of a cursed church, goes down into the labyrinth beneath it, and faces the first room-by-room exploration. The door is also their way back, along with stairways deep below that open to the town.
premise: A town that built its faith on a church + a door that now leads down into a labyrinth of increasingly vicious monsters = a sacred place that serves as the way into hell.

sensory.physical_environment: A church in Tristram whose front door opens onto the way down. Below it lies a labyrinth explored room by room.
sensory.behaviors: Delvers pass through the door and descend. Stairways deep within the dungeon open back to the town.
sensory.relationships: It stands in Tristram and connects the town to the labyrinth. It is the surface end of the route that leads down through the Catacombs.
sensory.attitudes: A cursed holy place, where faith has been turned into a threshold.
sensory.values: Passage, thresholds, and the memory of a sacred purpose now corrupted.

establishment.name: Tristram
establishment.worldview: The town wants the church and its descent managed and its people kept safe.
establishment.leverage: It controls the surface side of the entrance and the supplies delvers need.
establishment.flaw: It cannot close the door or defend itself against what comes up.

main_opponent.name: The labyrinth's monsters
main_opponent.worldview: The door is an invitation, and each level below is another mouth.
main_opponent.leverage: Each level beneath the church is more vicious than the last.
main_opponent.flaw: They are bound to the depths, so the church door marks the limit of their reach.

thematic_shadow.name: The cathedral's lost faith
thematic_shadow.worldview: A holy place cannot be abandoned, even when it has been cursed.
thematic_shadow.leverage: Its sacred ground and purpose make it a powerful symbol to the town.
thematic_shadow.flaw: The curse has twisted it, and the sacred has become the gateway.

tertiary_outcast.name: A watcher at the church door
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Someone must see who goes in and who comes out.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Knows who has descended and when they were last seen.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Powerless to follow, and haunted by those who never returned.

output_dial.level_1: A quiet threshold. The door stands closed, and the descent is an ordinary decision.
output_dial.level_2: The church feels watched. Delvers go in and the labyrinth below is cleared room by room.
output_dial.level_3: Monsters press toward the stairways, and the church door is the town's last line.
output_dial.level_4: What lives below breaks out through the cathedral, and the town's sacred center becomes its doom.

threat_clocks.name: The curse spreads upward
threat_clocks.advances_when: The labyrinth below is left uncontested or its horrors grow.

threat_clocks.name: Breach at the threshold
threat_clocks.advances_when: Monsters follow retreating delvers up the stairways toward the town.

yields_resource: Access to the first level of the labyrinth, a safe return route to Tristram, and a clear sense of how the dungeon connects to the town.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The cathedral is the main entrance to the dungeon. Its front door leads to the first level of the labyrinth beneath it, where the party explores room by room. It is a holy place turned into a doorway, and the one link between the town and the horrors below.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Use it as the opening and closing scene of any delve. It consumes the party's readiness and feeds them into the dungeon. Stairways deep within the dungeon open back to Tristram, so it also marks the way home. An arrival goes well when the party prepares, learns what they can from the town, and treats the door as a decision. It goes badly when they descend carelessly or are chased back up with monsters on their heels.

title: The Dark Exile
summary: A tale recorded in tomes scattered through the game world, recounting the Dark Exile. The card gives only the existence of the story, so its content is left for the table to fill in.
standalone_fallback: The party finds a tome in a ruined library or crypt that tells of a banished figure. Reading it raises the question of who the exile was, why they were cast out, and whether anyone still wants the story kept hidden. Resolve it as a single scene of discovery and a choice about what to do with the knowledge.
premise: Characters who seek the truth behind a buried story + a tale whose teller and subject are both unclear = a hunt for an exile whose fate is still unsettled.

sensory.physical_environment: Worn tomes shelved or abandoned in dim chambers, their pages telling the story of the Dark Exile.
sensory.behaviors: Readers pore over the volumes and piece the account together from fragments.
sensory.relationships: The reader stands in relation to an absent exile known only through the written account.
sensory.attitudes: Curiosity mixed with unease about a figure labelled 'Dark'.
sensory.values: Remembered history and the preservation of stories in written form.

establishment.name: Keepers of the tomes
establishment.worldview: Written accounts should be preserved and interpreted by those entrusted with them.
establishment.leverage: They control access to the volumes and decide how the tale is read.
establishment.flaw: Their reading may be partial and their silence may hide inconvenient parts of the story.

main_opponent.name: Those who would suppress the tale
main_opponent.worldview: Some stories are dangerous and are better lost.
main_opponent.leverage: They can remove, burn, or discredit the tomes.
main_opponent.flaw: Their efforts draw attention to the very story they want forgotten.

thematic_shadow.name: The Dark Exile
thematic_shadow.worldview: Cast out and defined by others, the exile is known only through the tale.
thematic_shadow.leverage: The legend itself shapes how others act long after the exile's removal.
thematic_shadow.flaw: The exile cannot speak for themselves, and the account may be unreliable.

tertiary_outcast.name: A wandering reader of the tomes
tertiary_outcast.worldview: The tale belongs to anyone willing to read it.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: Independent, answerable to no keeper, and willing to share what they have pieced together.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Without standing, their interpretations are easy to dismiss.

output_dial.level_1: A tome is found and its tale of the Dark Exile is read as idle lore.
output_dial.level_2: The party gathers several volumes and begins to see the outline of the exile's story.
output_dial.level_3: The tale draws the attention of those who would suppress it, and the tomes become contested.
output_dial.level_4: The story's truth is lost or weaponized, leaving the party with a legend that reshapes how the exile is judged.

threat_clocks.name: The Tale Is Silenced
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party delays, or rivals gather and destroy the tomes.

yields_resource: Knowledge of the Dark Exile's story, which can serve as a lead, a rumor, or leverage with those who care about the tale.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The only canon support is that tomes in the game world tell the tale of the Dark Exile. Everything else here, including the keepers, the suppressors and the outcast reader, is a judgement offered to give the table something to play with. Treat the exile's identity and fate as open.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place in a library, crypt, or sanctum as a quiet lore beat between action scenes. It consumes a discovery scene and feeds rumors, quests, or a later confrontation with whoever the exile turns out to be. Arrival goes well if the party reads carefully and shares or guards the knowledge with purpose. It goes badly if they treat the tomes as loot, or let a rival take the volumes and the narrative with them.

title: Dark Riders and Ritual at the Ruined Cathedral
summary: Townsfolk report an invasion by dark riders and strange rituals in the ruined cathedral at the edge of town, but the true nature of the evil is not yet clear.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a mystery seed. The party hears conflicting accounts of riders and ritual, then must decide what the evil really is by investigating the cathedral.
premise: A witness who saw something terrible but cannot name it + a threat that is only rumor = a party that must investigate before it can act

sensory.physical_environment: A ruined cathedral at the edge of town, a place of strange rituals.
sensory.behaviors: An anxious, dwindling populace speaks of invasion by dark riders and of rituals.
sensory.relationships: Townsfolk are bound by shared fear, and the riders and ritualists are known only by hearsay.
sensory.attitudes: Anxiety and uncertainty. The evil is not immediately clear in nature.
sensory.values: Safety and the need to understand what is hunting them.

establishment.name: The anxious townsfolk
establishment.worldview: Something is invading and the cathedral is at the heart of it.
establishment.leverage: They saw and heard the signs and can point the party toward the cathedral.
establishment.flaw: Their reports are fearful, secondhand and possibly contradictory.

main_opponent.name: The dark riders
main_opponent.worldview: The town is theirs to invade.
main_opponent.leverage: They have already driven the populace to fear and shrinkage.
main_opponent.flaw: Their nature and goals are unknown, so the party may misjudge them.

thematic_shadow.name: The cathedral ritualists
thematic_shadow.worldview: The ruined sacred place can still be turned to a dark purpose.
thematic_shadow.leverage: They control the unknown ritual, and the cathedral's holy ruin gives it weight.
thematic_shadow.flaw: Their rites are only rumor, so no one knows whether they are the cause or a symptom.

tertiary_outcast.name: A witness who saw too much
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Telling the truth will only bring the riders sooner.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: They may hold the one detail that clarifies the evil.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Fear keeps them silent or unreliable.

output_dial.level_1: Whispers of riders and odd rites circulate, and the town is uneasy but still functioning.
output_dial.level_2: Several townsfolk give overlapping but incomplete accounts, and the cathedral becomes the obvious focus.
output_dial.level_3: The rumors harden into fear, people avoid the cathedral edge of town, and misreadings of the evil start to cause harm.
output_dial.level_4: The riders and the ritual are no longer rumor but present horror, and the town has no clear answer for what it faces.

threat_clocks.name: The evil stays unnamed
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party acts on rumor without investigating or comparing accounts

yields_resource: A working hypothesis about the evil, a lead to the cathedral, and local trust when the party shares what it finds.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The evil haunting the village is not immediately clear in nature. All the town can say is that dark riders have invaded and strange rituals are happening in the ruined cathedral at the edge of town. The module is about turning fearful hearsay into understanding.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Use it as a clue layer within the opening arrival or as a follow-up in town. It consumes the villagers' willingness to talk and feeds the descent into the dungeon with a sense of mystery. Arrival goes well when the party compares accounts, notices the gaps, and enters the cathedral with questions rather than a ready answer. It goes badly if the GM resolves the mystery early, or if the party writes off the rumors as flavor.

title: The Diablo Dungeon
summary: The dungeon beneath Tristram, descended level by level. Its monsters are sorted by depth, from Goat Demons and Bats near the top to Acid Beasts, Overlords and Balrogs in the lower reaches. The Knights wait near the bottom.
standalone_fallback: Run it as a one-shot delve. The party descends through tiers of worsening monsters toward a bottom guarded by magic-resistant Knights. Each tier is a new threat family, and a way back up is the only safe resource.
premise: Heroes who must descend to end a threat + a dungeon whose monsters grow deadlier and more magic-proof with depth = a delve that punishes anyone who relies on one trick.

sensory.physical_environment: A dungeon of stacked levels. The upper levels hold Goat Demons and Bats, the middle and lower levels hold Acid Beasts and Vipers, and the deepest reaches hold Overlords, Magma Demons, Gargoyles and Balrogs. The bottom is the domain of the Knights.
sensory.behaviors: Monsters are grouped by depth, so each descent brings a new family of foes. Some inhabitants remain hidden until the party is among them.
sensory.relationships: The dungeon lies under Tristram and contains the Knights. Horned Demons are first expected a little below the early levels.
sensory.attitudes: Every level is hostile. The deeper levels feel more final and more resistant to the party's usual methods.
sensory.values: Depth is the measure of danger. The Knights at the bottom resist nearly every kind of magic, so brute persistence and varied tactics matter more than one favored spell.

establishment.name: The Knights
establishment.worldview: The bottom of the dungeon is theirs to hold, and they cannot be harmed by ordinary sorcery.
establishment.leverage: They resist virtually every type of magic.
establishment.flaw: They are found only at the bottom, so they cannot react to what happens higher up.

main_opponent.name: The Balrogs and Overlords
main_opponent.worldview: The deep levels belong to the strong, and intruders are prey.
main_opponent.leverage: They hold the lower depths where the surface has no reach.
main_opponent.flaw: They are tied to their depth and are not expected near the entrance.

thematic_shadow.name: The Acid Beasts
thematic_shadow.worldview: Attrition is enough. Anything that comes down will be worn away.
thematic_shadow.leverage: They are common in the mid-to-lower levels, where the party's supplies are already thin.
thematic_shadow.flaw: They are a mid-depth hazard and can be bypassed or prepared for by anyone who has scouted ahead.

tertiary_outcast.name: The hidden things of the dungeon
tertiary_outcast.worldview: Unseen things strike only when the moment is right.
tertiary_outcast.leverage: They stay concealed until the party has committed to a level.
tertiary_outcast.flaw: Their reliance on surprise fails once they are anticipated.

output_dial.level_1: The upper levels are grim but manageable: Goat Demons and Bats harry the party, and the way back to the surface is still short.
output_dial.level_2: Mid-depth monsters such as Vipers and Acid Beasts press the party. Supplies and healing run down, and each new level demands a different approach.
output_dial.level_3: The deep levels bring Overlords, Magma Demons and Balrogs. The party is cut off from the surface and forced to commit to the descent.
output_dial.level_4: At the bottom the Knights shrug off the party's magic and hold the final approach. Retreat is nearly impossible, and the party survives only by a hard-won change of tactics.

threat_clocks.name: The Descent Deepens
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party goes down a level, or lingers on one long enough for its inhabitants to gather.

threat_clocks.name: The Knights Awaken
threat_clocks.advances_when: The party reaches the lower levels or makes noise near the bottom.

yields_resource: Clearing a depth tier gives safer passage, knowledge of that tier's monster family, and access to the next level. Reaching the bottom gives the objective the dungeon guards.

sections.heading: Core Premise
sections.text: The Diablo dungeon is a vertical gauntlet beneath Tristram. Its inhabitants are sorted by depth, from Goat Demons and Bats near the top, through Vipers, Gargoyles and Acid Beasts in the middle, to Overlords, Magma Demons and Balrogs in the deep. The Knights sit near the bottom and resist virtually every type of magic. The dungeon rewards variety and punishes dependence on one trick.

sections.heading: GM Placement & Synergies
sections.text: Place it directly under Tristram as the main adventure site. It consumes the party's supplies, healing and resolve, and it feeds the surface settlement with news, relics and dread. Introduce each depth tier as a distinct encounter family. Horned Demons should appear a little below the early levels. An arrival goes well when the party has scouted, kept a retreat open and mixed physical and magical options. It goes badly when the party relies on magic alone against the Knights, or presses into the deep without supplies.
